questions.prompt: A service needs cacheable resources, client-selected dashboards, typed operations, a live channel and later notifications. What should the design compare?

options.label: Record separate resource-style, RPC, query-shape, channel and callback contracts.
Pick one label and assume it supplies every delivery and security rule.
Rank all labels by one universal speed order.

questions.explanation: These requirements describe different architectural, schema, RPC, channel and callback contracts. They can coexist; transport choice alone does not define permission or durable effect semantics.

questions.prompt: An office client selects one intermediary; the library exposes another in front of its services. Which distinction matters?

options.label: Both are defined only by which has more backends.
Every proxy necessarily anonymizes all traffic.
The forward proxy is client-selected; the reverse intermediary represents an origin service.

questions.explanation: The client-chosen forward proxy and origin-facing reverse intermediary represent different roles. A process may implement several functions, so trace whose authority is used on each hop.

questions.prompt: A dashboard requests two GraphQL fields for a book. Which review remains necessary?

options.label: A schema-valid query is always within the permitted work budget.
Authorize the requested resources and bound query work independently of the selected fields.
Two fields guarantee two cheap reads and automatic authorization.

questions.explanation: Response shape does not establish resource permission or resolver cost. Authorize the objects and bound work, expansion and deadlines separately from schema validation.

questions.prompt: The server stores result version 8, but its reply arrives after the client deadline. What follows?

options.label: A deadline failure does not prove that the server made no change.
The client can conclude that no result was stored.
Cancellation rolls back every earlier side effect.

questions.explanation: Client and server observations can differ. Earlier changes are not undone merely by cancellation; reconciliation and a stable operation identity are needed before an uncertain write is repeated.

questions.prompt: The gateway terminates TLS and routes to a healthy service. What is still unproven?

options.label: No other correctness rule is needed after a health check.
A gateway label means every user owns every requested object.
Routing and TLS termination do not establish durable application effects or user authorization.

questions.explanation: TLS protects the relevant connection and routing selects an eligible target. User/resource authorization and the destination's durable operation receipt require separate evidence.
